description: Draw ANY number of 2D primitives from one node — add a row per kind (Polygon, Circle, Stroke), each with its own colour, layer and input endpoint. The drawing counterpart of Input Properties.
instructions:
One node for the whole 2D output of an operation. Press "Add primitive" for a row, pick its KIND, and wire the geometry into that row's own `valin-<rowId>` endpoint on the left. Everything that is not a number — colour, layer name — lives on the row, because a Math Engine can only put numbers on a wire.

A ROW IS A STYLE GROUP, NOT A SHAPE. Fed a list with many entries, one row draws many pieces in its colour and layer, so a computed result of any size needs ONE row — not one node per shape. That is what replaces a chain of Polygon nodes.

KINDS
• POLYGON — takes a vertex list. `[[x,y],…]` is one outline; `[[[x,y],…],…]` is several; and a FLAT list whose rows carry a THIRD column splits into one outline per run of equal third value (the group column a Math Engine emits with `hcat(pts, fill(rows(pts),1,i))`). Vertex counts may differ from piece to piece. A grouped list is read EVEN-ODD, so a ring nested inside another is a HOLE rather than a second filled patch — which is what makes the Math Engine's `subtract(outline, cutters)` drawable directly: an outer boundary plus its holes arrives as one grouped list and draws with the holes voided. Disjoint rings still fill individually. A STROKE row is deliberately NOT read this way: its bands are independent quads, and two that overlapped would cancel instead of merging.
• CIRCLE — takes a CENTRE list and draws one circle per point: `[[x,y],…]` at the row's Radius, or `[[x,y,r],…]` to give every circle its own radius from the third column. Circles are emitted as sampled outlines (64 segments), so they behave like any other Space downstream.

• STROKE — takes a SEGMENT list `[[x1,y1,x2,y2],…]` and thickens each segment into a band of the row's Width about its centreline; a FIFTH column gives a segment its own width, exactly as Circle's third column gives a circle its own radius. The open-path row: Polygon and Circle can only draw a CLOSED ring, so a centreline — a frame member, a pipe run, a bar, a 3D Tube's plan projection — had to be widened into a quad by hand before it could be drawn. Segments are stroked INDEPENDENTLY, with no join between them: for a continuous mitred outline use the Mitered Join node. A zero-length segment is dropped rather than drawn as a spike, which is what a vertical 3D member projects to in plan.
COORDINATES are anchor-relative metres — the same frame `val-points` uses everywhere else, so a Space source's outline, a Math Engine's result and a Polygon node's echo all drop straight in.

EACH ROW ALSO PUBLISHES what it resolved on `val-<rowId>`, so a rendered piece can still feed a Boolean 2D, a Merge or another operation.

LAYER: names the canvas layer this row's pieces are rendered on (Flow Live). Blank falls back to the node's own layer. Several rows may share one name.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT REPLACE: the single-purpose generators (Rectangle, Ngon, Ellipse …). Those are for hand-authoring, where a width/height slider is the point. This node is for geometry that arrives computed.
